title: Atlas descent and algebraic structures on enlarged etale sheaves
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with every site small relative to its sheaves. Use chartwise etale morphisms as in [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]: every representable etale scheme chart remains representable etale after composition. For a space $A$, let $\mathcal C_A$ have objects chartwise etale maps $T\to A$ from algebraic spaces, arrows all maps over $A$, and coverings jointly surjective chartwise etale families [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. Write $i_A:A_{\mathrm{et}}\to\mathcal C_A$ for the scheme-object inclusion, regarding schemes as their representable sheaves [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space]. Let $X$ be a space and $F$ a sheaf of sets on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$. There exists a sheaf $E$ on $\mathcal C_X$ with a specified isomorphism $e:i_X^*E\simeq F$. For any two such pairs $(E,e),(E',e')$, there is exactly one isomorphism $a:E\simeq E'$ with $e'\circ i_X^*a=e$. For every object $T\to X$ and every surjective representable etale scheme chart $T_0\to T$, the overlap $T_1=T_0\times_TT_0$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] is a scheme and restriction, followed by $e$, identifies $E(T)$ with $\operatorname{Eq}(F(T_0)\rightrightarrows F(T_1))$. These identifications commute with restriction along every $T'\to T$, after chart refinement, are independent of the chosen charts, and are natural in $F$. Restriction preserves finite products and terminal objects. It induces an equivalence on sheaves of commutative rings, and for any ring sheaf $R$ on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ and any normalized ring-sheaf extension $(\widetilde R,e_R)$, an equivalence $\operatorname{Mod}(\widetilde R)\simeq\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Under this equivalence the addition, zero, inverse, scalar action, restriction semilinearity and linearity of morphisms are the ones obtained by uniquely extending the corresponding operations on the scheme subsite. In particular $\mathcal O_X$ has a normalized ring-sheaf extension $\widetilde{\mathcal O}_X$, with the same atlas equalizer formula as a ring.

source.place: Tag 03H7 (remark-explain-equivalence); paragraph after Tag 03G7 (definition-structure-sheaf). Transport of ring and module operations expands this comparison using the sectionwise sheaf definitions.

proof.text: Extract full faithfulness, singleton scheme atlases, finite limits, and cocontinuity from scheme density. The singleton atlases give cover density; cocontinuity and continuity show that covering sieves are reflected and preserved. Since each covering atlas has one member, Mathlib IsOneHypercoverDense.of_hasPullbacks gives one-hypercover density with indexing universe zero. Apply isEquivalence_of_isOneHypercoverDense for every coefficient category with finite limits, including sets and commutative rings. For normalized set extensions use an object preimage, and lift e.hom followed by the inverse normalization by full faithfulness. Lift morphisms in the same way; naturality gives the section formula, and faithfulness proves uniqueness.

Use representable etale scheme tests to represent the pullback of a chart against a scheme object. Compose its etale projection with the structure map to obtain a small-site scheme object. Yoneda full faithfulness gives the scheme arrows and reflects the pullback square. Base change of surjectivity gives a surjective first projection. For a surjective etale scheme chart, a field-valued point lifts after extension to the residue field of a point of its nonempty scheme fibre. Thus the chart is a singleton covering of the enlarged site. Apply the singleton-cover sheaf gluing and separation conditions; the pullback square expresses precisely equality of the two overlap restrictions. Transport through the specified normalization to obtain the equalizer bijection, whose formula determines it uniquely.

source.place: Tag 03H7 (remark-explain-equivalence), displayed equalizer and the following sentence; site sheaf condition Tag 00VR (sites.tex).

proof.text: For a map between enlarged objects, pull back the original chart against the new scheme chart using the preceding scheme-test construction. Its projection is surjective etale, hence a singleton covering in the small site. The small-site sheaf separation condition makes restriction along this projection injective. Naturality of the normalization and the pullback square give the required formula on the refinement. This proves restriction compatibility and chart independence. The morphism-lifting formula from the first step gives naturality in the sheaf.

source.place: Tag 03H7 (remark-explain-equivalence), equalizer, with the chart-refinement and naturality checks written out.

proof.text: Restriction on set sheaves is an equivalence by the first step. Every equivalence preserves finite products, including the empty product, so obtain the stated preservation instance directly from Mathlib.

Apply the arbitrary-coefficient comparison from the first step to CommRingCat. Its finite limits are already supplied by Mathlib, so restriction on commutative-ring sheaves is an equivalence without separately constructing ring objects.

source.place: Section 00YR (section-sheaves-algebraic-structures), commutative ring objects and the proof of Tag 00YV (proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi).

proof.text: For the given ring extension first lift an arbitrary small-site module as an abelian-group sheaf using the coefficient comparison for Ab. Lift the scalar action as a map of set sheaves through the fully faithful set restriction. The scalar ring universe is independent of the module universe: lift its underlying sets by ULift, and prove these remain sheaves by identifying ring elements with homomorphisms from the free ring on one generator. Evaluate the lifted action at each scalar and section. All module laws follow after restriction by faithfulness; cover density makes the forgetful functor to underlying set sheaves faithful. Naturality of the action gives linear restrictions. Lift morphisms through the abelian-group equivalence and use the same faithful comparison to prove scalar linearity. This proves full faithfulness and essential surjectivity of module restriction. Finally compose with transport along the specified ring normalization, using Mathlib pushforwardComp and pushforwardPushforwardEquivalence. The displayed addition, inverse, scalar, restriction and morphism formulas follow from the actual pushforward definitions and map_smul. The last hom-set bijection is the set comparison again.

source.place: Tag 03CV (definition-sheaf-modules); explicit operation lifting along the equivalence of Tag 03G1 (spaces-properties.tex).

proof.text: Forget a commutative-ring extension to sets, lifting the underlying set universe by ULift so the atlas equalizer applies. The restriction followed by normalization is a ring homomorphism into the chart ring. The pullback relation makes its values belong to the equalizer subring. The set equalizer proves this homomorphism bijective, so RingEquiv.ofBijective gives the desired ring isomorphism and formula. For the structure sheaf use its existing normalized restriction isomorphism, whose scheme sections are the actual rings of regular functions.
